repair_candidates.title: Run a focused Local Network trace while opening System Settings
repair_candidates.risk: Low: read-only logging and filesystem observation; sudo may be requested by macOS for fs_usage/lsof visibility.
repair_candidates.manual_action: Run the trace command, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network, wait 20–30 seconds, then stop the trace.
repair_candidates.expected_result: The trace should identify whether SecurityPrivacyExtension, LaunchServices .csstore reads, TCC/REG, or another privacy cache is feeding the stale GUI entry.
repair_candidates.fallback_branch: If the trace still does not identify a safe repair, collect a full read-only bundle with mse collect and inspect the generated evidence before proposing any higher-risk action.

repair_candidates.title: Manually reinstall Google Chrome from a fresh download
repair_candidates.risk: Low to medium: user-driven app reinstall; bookmarks/profile data should remain in the Chrome profile, but the tool will not remove or edit any files.
repair_candidates.manual_action: Quit Chrome normally, download Chrome from Google, install it into /Applications, reboot, and open Chrome once. Do not use this tool to remove app bundles or profiles.
repair_candidates.expected_result: A fresh signed /Applications registration should replace code-sign-clone or orphaned LaunchServices records as the active Chrome identity.
repair_candidates.fallback_branch: If Local Network still shows the same broken Chrome state, continue with branch 3: capture a focused trace.
